noteBlocks.lede: Trout on a fish farm have lengths that follow a normal curve. What fraction are longer than 40.5 cm? One subtraction and one division turn 40.5 into a z-score, the printed table turns the z-score into an area, and a quick sketch tells you whether that area is the answer or 1 minus it.

Use the symmetry of the curve when the value is below the mean

noteBlocks.text: How many trout are longer than 40.5 cm?

noteBlocks.md:
On a fish farm the trout have lengths that are normally distributed with mean 34 cm and standard deviation 5 cm. The fraction longer than 40.5 cm is the area under the curve to the right of 40.5.
The whole area under the curve is 1, so that shaded area is a probability, $P(L > 40.5)$.

noteBlocks.alt: A bell-shaped curve over a horizontal axis. Under the axis, the mean 34 cm with z = 0 under it, and 40.5 cm with z = 1.30 under it. The region under the curve to the right of 40.5 is shaded and labelled P(L > 40.5) above the curve.
noteBlocks.caption: The mean sits under the peak. The values and their z-scores go under the axis; only the shaded area goes above it.

noteBlocks.prompt: On the trout curve, which way from 40.5 cm does the shaded region go?
options: To the right, towards longer trout
To the left, towards shorter trout
noteBlocks.answer: To the right, towards longer trout
noteBlocks.explain: The question is about trout longer than 40.5 cm, so the region runs to the right of 40.5, out into the tail.

noteBlocks.md:
Every normal curve has the same shape; only its centre and its spread change. The z-score measures a value in standard deviations from the mean:
$z = \frac{x - \mu}{\sigma}$
Subtract the mean to find how far $x$ is from the middle, then divide by the standard deviation to count that distance in standard deviations.

noteBlocks.md: $z = \frac{x - \mu}{\sigma}$ is not on the Unit 3 formula sheet. $\mu$ is the mean and $\sigma$ the standard deviation. A value below the mean gives a negative $z$.

noteBlocks.prompt: Trout lengths have mean 34 cm and standard deviation 5 cm. What is the z-score of a trout 29.5 cm long?
noteBlocks.explain:
$z = \frac{29.5 - 34}{5}$
$= \frac{-4.5}{5}$
$= -0.9$. The minus sign says 29.5 cm is below the mean.

noteBlocks.md: Find the row for $z$ to one decimal place, then move across to the column for the second decimal place. For $z = 1.30$ that is row 1.3, column .00: $\Phi(1.30) = 0.9032$, the ringed entry.

noteBlocks.prompt: Using the table extract with rows 1.1 to 1.4, what is $\Phi(1.24)$?
noteBlocks.explain: Row 1.2, column .04: $\Phi(1.24) = 0.8925$, the area to the left of $z = 1.24$.

noteBlocks.alt: A normal curve with the right-hand tails beyond z = 1, 2 and 3 shaded more and more darkly, and under each z the share of the curve beyond it: 16%, 2.3%, 0.13%.
noteBlocks.caption: The share of the curve beyond z = 1, 2 and 3: numbers to hold an answer against before writing it down.

noteBlocks.md: About 68% of a normal distribution lies within one standard deviation of the mean, so each tail beyond $z = 1$ holds about 16%. About 95% lies within two, so a tail beyond $z = 2$ holds roughly 2.5%; the table makes it 2.3%. Compare every answer with these before you write it down.

noteBlocks.prompt: Roughly what fraction of a normal curve lies in the right-hand tail beyond $z = 2.1$?
noteBlocks.explain:
Beyond $z = 2$ is about 2.3%, and 2.1 is a little further out: $1 - \Phi(2.1) = 1 - 0.9821$
$= 0.0179$, about 1.8%. The 98% is $\Phi(2.1)$, the area to the left.

noteBlocks.md: The table only ever gives the area to the left. So draw the curve, mark $x$ and its $z$ under the axis, and shade the region the question asks for. Then decide.

noteBlocks.alt: Two small curves. On the left one the region to the left of z is shaded, labelled P(Z < z) = Φ(z). On the right one the region to the right of z is shaded, labelled P(Z > z) = 1 − Φ(z).
noteBlocks.caption: Shaded to the left: read the table. Shaded to the right: take the table value from 1.

noteBlocks.md: Shaded to the left, the answer is $\Phi(z)$. Shaded to the right, the answer is $1 - \Phi(z)$, because the whole area is 1.

noteBlocks.title: The mark most often dropped
noteBlocks.md: Examiners have reported candidates who found $z$ correctly and then gave the table value where 1 minus it was needed, and they noted that a sketch with $x$ and $z$ under the axis made full marks far more likely.

noteBlocks.prompt: Trout lengths have mean 34 cm and standard deviation 5 cm, and $\Phi(1.3) = 0.9032$. What is $P(L > 40.5)$?
noteBlocks.explain:
Shaded to the right, so $1 - \Phi(1.3) = 1 - 0.9032$
$= 0.0968$. Giving 0.9032 would say that most trout are longer than 40.5 cm.

noteBlocks.alt: Two curves, one above the other. On the upper curve the left tail below z = −0.60 is shaded and labelled P(Z < −0.60). On the lower curve the right tail above z = 0.60 is shaded and labelled P(Z > 0.60). A box between them says same area, by symmetry.
noteBlocks.caption: Fold the curve at the mean and one tail lands on the other.

noteBlocks.md:
The table stops at $z = 0$ because the curve is symmetric about its mean. The left tail below $-z$ is the mirror image of the right tail above $z$, so the two areas are equal:
$P(Z < -z) = P(Z > z)$
$= 1 - \Phi(z)$
For a trout shorter than 31 cm, $z = \frac{31 - 34}{5}$
$= -0.6$.

noteBlocks.title: Why it is 1 minus
noteBlocks.md: $\Phi(0.6)$ is everything to the left of $+0.6$. Fold the tail below $-0.6$ across the mean and it lands exactly on the tail above $+0.6$, which is everything except $\Phi(0.6)$.

noteBlocks.prompt: Trout lengths have mean 34 cm and standard deviation 5 cm, and $\Phi(0.6) = 0.7257$. Work out $P(L < 31)$.
noteBlocks.explain:
$z = -0.6$, a left tail below a negative $z$: $1 - \Phi(0.6) = 1 - 0.7257$
$= 0.2743$. Leaving 0.7257 would say most trout are shorter than 31 cm, and the sketch shows only a thin tail.

noteBlocks.text: Above a value below the mean

noteBlocks.alt: A normal curve with 29.5 cm marked below the mean 34 cm, z = −0.90 under it, and everything to the right of 29.5 shaded, more than half of the curve, labelled P(L > 29.5).
noteBlocks.caption: More than half is shaded, so the answer is more than 0.5.

noteBlocks.md:
When $x$ is below the mean and you want the area above it, more than half of the curve is shaded. By the same symmetry, $P(Z > -z)$ is $P(Z < z)$, which is $\Phi(z)$: read the table and stop.
The sketch keeps you honest here. If more than half is shaded, the answer must be more than 0.5.

noteBlocks.prompt: Trout lengths have mean 34 cm and standard deviation 5 cm, and $\Phi(0.9) = 0.8159$. What is $P(L > 29.5)$?
noteBlocks.explain:
$z = -0.9$ and the area above it is the mirror image of the area below $+0.9$: $P(L > 29.5) = \Phi(0.9)$
$= 0.8159$. Taking it from 1 would give 0.1841, less than a half, which the sketch rules out.

noteBlocks.md: **Question.** Trout lengths have mean 34 cm and standard deviation 5 cm. Find the probability that a trout is longer than 43 cm. Give your answer to 4 decimal places.

**Line 1.** $z = \frac{43 - 34}{5}$
**Line 2.** $= 1.8$. The first two marks are for these two lines.
**Line 3.** Sketch: 43 cm is above the mean, so shade to the right.
**Line 4.** $P(L > 43) = 1 - \Phi(1.8)$
**Line 5.** $= 1 - 0.9641$
**Line 6.** $= 0.0359$

noteBlocks.title: Master Normal Distribution in minutes!
noteBlocks.why: A Northern Ireland tutor on normal-distribution probabilities for CCEA. As you watch, make the decision yourself before each answer appears: which side is shaded, and is the table value the answer or 1 minus it?

noteBlocks.prompt: Trout lengths have mean 34 cm and standard deviation 5 cm, and $\Phi(0.6) = 0.7257$. Work out $P(L < 37)$ to 4 decimal places.
noteBlocks.explain:
$z = \frac{37 - 34}{5}$
$= 0.6$. The region is shaded to the left, so the answer is $\Phi(0.6) = 0.7257$ itself, with nothing taken from 1.

noteBlocks.md: **More than a value below the mean.** The second part in 2024, 2025 and 2026. More than half the curve is shaded, so the answer is over 0.5: read $\Phi$ at the positive $z$ and stop.
**Given that.** 2022 and 2023 ended with less than one value, given less than a larger one. Everything below the smaller value is also below the larger, so divide one tail by the other.

noteBlocks.prompt: Plant heights are normally distributed, with $P(H < 150) = 0.2$ and $P(H < 170) = 0.8$. What is the probability that a plant is shorter than 150 cm, given that it is shorter than 170 cm?
noteBlocks.explain: Every plant under 150 cm is also under 170 cm, so the top of the fraction is $P(H < 150)$ itself: $\frac{0.2}{0.8} = 0.25$. Multiplying 0.2 by 0.8 treats the two heights as independent, and they are not.

noteBlocks.md: **Units that do not match.** 2026 gave a mean in minutes and asked about a number of hours. Convert first, then standardise: 2 hours is 120 minutes.
**Words that change the tail.** 'Or over' and 'does not qualify' decide the shading, not the method (2021). For a measurement, 'or over' and 'more than' give the same probability.

noteBlocks.prompt: Delivery times have mean 48 minutes and standard deviation 8 minutes. A question asks for the probability that a delivery does not take more than 1 hour. Which first line is right?
noteBlocks.explain: An hour is 60 minutes, so standardise 60, not 1: $z = 1.5$. 'Does not take more than' is the region to the left of 60, so the answer is read straight from the table: $\Phi(1.5) = 0.9332$.

noteBlocks.md:
Standardise with $z = \frac{x - \mu}{\sigma}$, which is not on the formula sheet.
Read $\Phi(z)$: the row for the first decimal place, the column for the second.
Sketch and shade first, then choose $\Phi(z)$ or $1 - \Phi(z)$, folding the curve for a negative $z$.
For 'given that', divide one tail by the other.
Check an answer against 16% beyond one standard deviation and 2.3% beyond two.

The normal question sits in the middle of Unit 3: usually two parts of 3 or 4 marks, each a probability above or below one value, to 4 decimal places, and in 2022 and 2023 a 2-mark 'given that' to finish. The first two marks are for the z-value, then one for the shading or the 1 minus decision, and the last for the answer. Stuck? Sketch and shade: the picture shows the next step.

items.stem: Which area does $\Phi(z)$ in the Normal Probability Table give?

options.text: The area to the left of z

options.text: The area to the left of −z

prompts.prompt: The formula that turns a value x into a z-score, and what its letters mean.
prompts.answer: z = (x − μ)/σ, where μ is the mean and σ the standard deviation. It is not on the formula sheet.

prompts.prompt: What does Φ(z) in the Normal Probability Table give?
prompts.answer: The area under the standard normal curve to the left of z, which is P(Z < z).

prompts.prompt: How do you find P(X > x) when x is above the mean?
prompts.answer: Find z, sketch the curve and shade to the right of x, then work out 1 − Φ(z).

prompts.prompt: How do you find P(X < x) when x is below the mean, so that z is negative?
prompts.answer: By symmetry the left tail below a negative z equals the right tail above the positive value, so the answer is 1 − Φ of the positive z. Leaving Φ as the answer is the slip examiners report.

prompts.prompt: What is P(X > x) when x is below the mean, and why must it be more than 0.5?
prompts.answer: It is Φ of the positive z, read straight from the table; more than half the curve is shaded, so it must be more than 0.5.

prompts.prompt: On a normal sketch, what goes below the axis and what goes above it?
prompts.answer: Below the axis: the mean, the value x and their z-values. Above it: only the shaded area, which is the probability.

prompts.prompt: Which normal probabilities does this specification ask for, and which does it not?
prompts.answer: Single tails only, above or below one value, found from a z-value. Never the area between two values, and never a z-value from a probability.

prompts.prompt: How do you find the probability that X is less than a, given that X is less than b, when a is smaller than b?
prompts.answer: Divide: P(X < a) ÷ P(X < b). Every value below a is also below b, so the top of the fraction is P(X < a) itself; multiplying the two probabilities is the slip examiners report.
